- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75%), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model often underestimates downside; add 2–3% buffer below historical low.  
- When sentiment alternates between bullish/bearish (e.g., 0.33/1.00 cycles), model overfits short-term momentum; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model often fails to capture event-driven volatility; increase forecast variance by ±1.5% of recent 7-day range.  
- If sentiment is bearish and price is trending up, model may misread sentiment; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment <0.33.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates mean reversion after spikes; add 1–2% downward bias if price >75% above 30-day MA.
